title: Mastering CSS z-index
summary: This lesson explains the fundamental rules of CSS z-index, including the requirement for positioning and the concept of stacking contexts. It also introduces the isolation property and visual debugging tools in Chrome DevTools to resolve layering bugs.

transcript.text: Your dropdown hides behind the modal.
Rule one, z-index only works on position elements: relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky.
Without position, your z-index is completely ignored by the browser.
Rule two, every stacking context is its own universe.
A child with z-index 9999 still sits below a sibling context with z-index 1.
One line creates a new stacking context with no position required.
Perfect for reusable components that should never leak z-index into the rest of your app.
Chrome DevTools has a layers panel that shows every stacking context in three dimensions.
Debug visually instead of spraying z-index 9000 everywhere.
Save this for your next z-index bug. Follow for more front-end deep dives.

before_after: A dropdown menu incorrectly hidden behind a modal window is resolved by understanding stacking contexts and positioning rules.
